pages.text: Several machines are built by $(item)sequenced assembly$(), with a winding step in the loop. Put a Winding Machine on the belt line, with the right spool mounted, where the sequence asks for winding.
$(li)$(item)Electric Motor$(): starts from a shaft, 3 loops. The winding step takes $(item)75 turns$() of a $(item)Copper Spool$(), then a magnet, a steel mechanism and a screwdriver.
$(li)$(item)Generator$(): starts from a shaft, 3 loops. Capacitor, steel plate, then $(item)75 turns$() of a $(item)Copper Spool$(), then a magnet, a steel mechanism and a screwdriver.

$(li)$(item)Potentiometer$(): starts from a Heavy Machinery Casing, 3 loops. $(item)100 turns$() of a $(item)Constantan Spool$(), then a steel cogwheel, copper wire and lubrication oil.$(br2)For these steps the target value box does not matter: the recipe sets the number of turns.

A winding step $(item)waits$() when the mounted spool is the wrong metal or out of turns. The item never skips the step, so a line that stops here usually just needs a fresh spool. A funnel can swap empty spools for full ones.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
